note: The error surface: which namespace each thrown or read type lives in, what SdkException and ApiError expose, and how RawError buffers and reads a body. These are what a catch ladder is built from.

assertions.claim: SdkException<TError> exposes a single property - `public required TError Error { get; init; }`, the parsed error model. Everything a catch block can read comes off `ex.Error`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Catch the exception, first line

assertions.claim: The throwing path carries NO HTTP status code and no response headers - `ex.StatusCode` does not exist. Only ApiResult exposes StatusCode/Headers, on both outcomes.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Result-style alternative, 'Unlike the throwing path, ApiResult exposes the HTTP StatusCode and Headers on both success and failure'

assertions.claim: Every exception type the SDK throws lives in {RootNamespace}.Core.Exceptions - SdkException<T>, AuthSchemeException and the three Sse* exceptions - so one using covers all of them, and none of them sits with ApiError/RawError under Core.ErrorResponse.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § the namespace list and § Notes (AuthSchemeException); dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, 'all under {RootNamespace}.Core.Exceptions'

assertions.claim: The ApiError base declares no typed TryGet* accessor of its own - a helper typed as `ApiError` can reach only TryGetRawError, which is why error-reading must not be factored out of the per-operation catch block.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, "Don't factor error-reading into a shared helper typed as ApiError"

assertions.claim: The base declares `bool TryGetRawError(out RawError error)` - the accessor every {Operation}Error inherits, and the reason a Case A catch that spells the out type needs the Core.ErrorResponse using.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, step 1, third bullet; dotnet-testing § Test an error path

assertions.claim: ApiError does not override ToString(), so `e.ToString()` on an error yields the bare type name rather than a message - the fallback a shared `Describe(ApiError e)` helper silently lands on.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, "Don't factor error-reading into a shared helper typed as ApiError" - 'falls back to e.ToString() - a bare type name'

assertions.claim: RawError sits with ApiError under {RootNamespace}.Core.ErrorResponse, NOT with SdkException under Core.Exceptions - so a Case B catch needs exactly those two usings, and Core.* is not one namespace.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § the namespace list, 'ApiError and RawError -> {RootNamespace}.Core.ErrorResponse'; § Case B, the two-using sample; dotnet-testing § Test an error path, Case B

assertions.claim: RawError is NOT an ApiError - it declares no base type at all, so nothing an ApiError-typed helper knows about applies to a Case B error.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § two shapes, Case B bullet; dotnet-testing § Test an error path, Case B

assertions.claim: RawError has no TryGet* and no TryGetRawError - in Case B `ex.Error` IS the RawError and is read directly.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case B - 'there are no TryGet* accessors and no TryGetRawError'; dotnet-testing § Test an error path, Case B

assertions.claim: RawError.StatusCode is a get-only HttpStatusCode carrying the failing response's status - which is why the samples write `(int)raw.StatusCode` and compare against `HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case B sample; dotnet-testing § Test an error path, the Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode...) line

assertions.claim: ReadAsBytes/ReadAsString/ReadAsJson<T> are synchronous - none returns a Task - so the samples call them without await, inside a catch block or an assertion.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case B sample; dotnet-testing § Test an error path, 'ex.Error.ReadAsString() / ex.Error.ReadAsJson<MyDto>()'

assertions.claim: ReadAsJson<T>() is a bare expression-bodied delegation to JsonSerializer.Deserialize with no try/catch - so it THROWS JsonException when the body isn't valid JSON, and a RawError body often isn't. Prefer ReadAsString().
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case B - 'ReadAsJson<T>() throws JsonException when the body isn't valid JSON'

assertions.claim: The error body is copied into a byte[] the RawError owns BEFORE the RawError exists, so ReadAsString()/ReadAsJson<T>() still work after the call returned and the HttpResponseMessage was disposed.
assertions.defends: dotnet-testing § Test an error path - the body assertions run after the throw

assertions.claim: RawError has no public constructor - you never build one, you read the one the SDK handed you on ex.Error.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case B - 'Its public members are StatusCode, ReadAsBytes/ReadAsString/ReadAsJson<T>'

assertions.claim: Every type under Errors/ is a `public sealed class {Operation}Error : ApiError` - which is what makes the inherited TryGetRawError available on all of them (Case A).
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § two shapes, Case A bullet; dotnet-testing § Test an error path - 'ex.Error is the typed ApiError'

assertions.claim: No {Operation}Error redeclares TryGetRawError - it is purely inherited, so it does NOT appear among the accessors you read off the class file, and a ladder built only from the accessors declared there would omit the final branch.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, step 1 third bullet ('the inherited TryGetRawError(out RawError), which every {Operation}Error exposes') and step 2

assertions.claim: Every accessor on an {Operation}Error is a `public bool TryGet...` - none returns the body, a nullable, or a Task, so a branch is always `if (ex.Error.TryGet...(...))`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, step 1 - 'They are the public bool TryGet...(out ...) methods on the {Operation}Error type'

assertions.claim: Each accessor takes exactly one `out` parameter and nothing else - there is no status argument and no overload to disambiguate, so `TryGet...(out var body)` is the whole call.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, step 1 and the catch template

assertions.claim: Each generated factory fills exactly ONE accessor slot and passes `default` for every other - so at most one TryGet* is ever true for a given response, and the if/else-if ladder never double-fires.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § 'Why TryGetRawError goes last - it is not a universal fallback'

assertions.claim: Every {Operation}Error's status switch ends in a `_ =>` arm that routes to the fallback factory - so a status the operation does not enumerate always lands in TryGetRawError rather than producing an error with every slot empty.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A template, 'ALWAYS LAST: fallback for untyped statuses only'

assertions.claim: No enumerated status arm routes to the fallback factory - only the unenumerated `_ =>` arm does. A status the operation maps explicitly, even one whose body is a raw RawError, therefore leaves TryGetRawError FALSE and must be read through its own accessor.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § 'Why TryGetRawError goes last' - 'The status-specific RawError accessors are likewise not surfaced by TryGetRawError'; dotnet-testing § Test an error path - 'Only statuses the operation maps to RawError populate TryGetRawError'

assertions.claim: A typed-body accessor is named after the body it yields - `TryGet{Body}(out {Body} value)`. The ONLY accessors whose name does not repeat the out type are the status-specific ones whose body is RawError, which are named after the response instead.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, step 1 - 'their names embed the body type', typed-body vs status-specific RawError bullets; dotnet-testing § Test an error path - 'its name embeds the body type'

assertions.claim: No {Operation}Error overrides ToString() either, so the bare-type-name fallback is what a caller actually gets - never a message worth putting on the wire.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Case A, the ApiError.ToString() bare-type-name trap

assertions.claim: An accessor slot reports true only when the generated factory filled it through Some(...); a slot left `default` reports false. That is the mechanism behind 'exactly one TryGet* fires' and behind TryGetRawError being false for a mapped status.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § 'Why TryGetRawError goes last - it is not a universal fallback'; dotnet-testing § Test an error path

assertions.claim: Nothing wraps the success-body deserialization: a 2xx whose body no longer matches the model surfaces as a raw System.Text.Json.JsonException, which matches NEITHER a catch (SdkException<...>) nor a transport catch.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Presenting failures at your boundary - 'A success status with a broken body is a third failure kind'

assertions.claim: The error body is deserialized to completion BEFORE the failure outcome (and therefore before any SdkException) exists - so when an {Operation}Error model disagrees with the body the API really sends, the JsonException REPLACES the SdkException and the HTTP status is gone with it.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § 'The same exception also arrives from the error path, and means the opposite'

assertions.claim: SseException is an abstract Exception base - catching SseException handles either streaming failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, Errors - 'both derive from a common SseException base (catch SseException to handle either)'

assertions.claim: Every concrete SSE exception derives from SseException - there is no streaming failure that a `catch (SseException)` misses.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, Errors - 'both derive from a common SseException base'

assertions.claim: SseTimeoutException carries `TimeSpan IdleTimeout` - the window that elapsed without a frame - so the catch block's `ex.IdleTimeout` resolves.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, 'SseTimeoutException.IdleTimeout reports the window that elapsed'

assertions.claim: A frame that fails to deserialize is rethrown as SseDeserializationException with the original JsonException as its InnerException - so `ex.InnerException` in the catch block is the JsonException, and only a JsonException is converted this way.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, Errors - 'carries the RawFrame text and the underlying JsonException as InnerException'

assertions.claim: SseDeserializationException carries the offending payload as `string RawFrame` - the catch block's `ex.RawFrame` resolves.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Streaming, the catch (SseDeserializationException ex) clause

assertions.claim: AuthSchemeException derives straight from Exception - it is NOT an SdkException<T>, so a catch (SdkException<...>) won't match it and it must be caught separately.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Notes, first bullet

assertions.claim: AuthSchemeException carries `IReadOnlyList<Exception> SchemeFailures` - the per-scheme failures, which is what the separate catch reads.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § Notes, first bullet - 'it carries IReadOnlyList<Exception> SchemeFailures'
